# Evaluation

All metrics are measured on the **61-day time-based hold-out**
(2025-11-01 to 2025-12-30). Nothing is reported on training data.

```{r eval}
pipe <- run_pipeline("../data/synthetic", "../data/processed")
daily <- pipe$daily
results <- list()
for (target in c("sla_attainment_pct", "tickets_received")) {
  bf <- build_features(daily, target, include_operational = FALSE)
  sp <- time_split(bf$frame, test_days = 61)
  ml <- train_ml_forecasters(sp$train[, bf$features, drop = FALSE],
                             sp$train[[target]])
  preds <- predict_ml(ml, sp$test[, bf$features, drop = FALSE])
  for (nm in names(preds)) {
    m <- regression_metrics(sp$test[[target]], preds[[nm]])
    results[[length(results) + 1]] <-
      data.frame(target = target, model = nm, mae = m$mae,
                 rmse = m$rmse, mape = m$mape)
  }
}
do.call(rbind, results)
```

## What "good" means here

- **MAPE under 5%** on SLA attainment is the bar: SLA is a
  slow-moving, bounded KPI (68–99.5%), so a model that cannot beat
  seasonal naive by a clear margin is not adding value.
- **Anomaly detection** is judged on F1 against the injected
  incidents — recall matters more than precision, because a missed
  bad feed corrupts every downstream report.
- **Driver ranking** is judged by stability: the top-3 drivers
  should be the same under permutation importance and under the
  STATA / SPSS / SAS standardised-coefficient replication.

## Honest limits

- Synthetic data: magnitudes and rankings are illustrative, not
  evidence about any real client.
- The STATA / SPSS / SAS scripts replicate the same data, splits
  and metrics but were not executed on this machine (commercial
  software not installed). Run them in the licensed application to
  reproduce the comparison table.
- A 14-day forecast degrades with horizon; the reported 14-day
  MAPE is the honest number, not the 1-step MAPE.
